answer: Each agent may submit a signed claim, but rewards are released only after a randomly selected peer has staked tokens on that agent’s useful work and the work survives a challenge period. A sybil can multiply identities, not independent stake: splitting funds across accounts leaves less backing each claim, while convincing peers to risk tokens requires real evidence. The attacker pays for scarce capital and may lose it when claims fail; the voyage of one false identity can send a costly ripple through the network, exposed by a prism of peer review.
